Iran and the U.S. traded heated rhetoric on social media after President Trump used vulgar language while threatening to target more of Iran's infrastructure if the country's leaders don't reopen the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday. The official X account for Iran’s Permanent Mission to the United Nations responded that Trump “seeks to drag the region into an endless war.” It added that his threat to target civilian infrastructure showed intent to commit a war crime and urged immediate international intervention. Mehdi Tabatabaei, deputy for communications and information in Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian's office, posted on X that President Trump had “resorted to obscenities and nonsense out of sheer desperation and anger.” He went on to use similarly insulting language, saying that the strait would open when Iran has been compensated for the cost of this war. President Donald Trump hosted a delegation of prominent Hasidic rabbis and a Litvish rosh yeshiva at the White House on Thursday, September 3, for a pre-Rosh Hashanah meeting. The delegation included leaders associated with Satmar, Bobov, Skver and Vizhnitz, along with Rabbi Malkiel Kotler of Lakewood’s Beth Medrash Govoha. The Skverer Rebbe was represented by his son.  The meeting focused on issues affecting Orthodox Jewish communities, including religious liberty and the independence of yeshiva education. The Israeli military draft of Haredi yeshiva students was also expected to be a topic of discussion, although reports differed on how central that issue would be.  The gathering was notable because some of the invited leaders, particularly those associated with Satmar, hold strongly anti-Zionist or non-Zionist positions. That aspect of the invitation drew criticism from some pro-Israel voices.  The meeting also had historical significance: a similar gathering of leading rabbis at the White House took place under President Jimmy Carter in 1979, nearly 47 years earlier.  #AfriVisionMedia #Trump #WhiteHouse #RoshHashanah #Judaism

President Donald Trump said Friday that he calls the Iran war a “military conflict” because he thinks it’s “small potatoes” for the United States. Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, Trump compared Iran to other wars by length and U.S. casualties — pointing out that 18 Americans have been killed there compared to “tens of thousands of people” in other conflicts. The president said the U.S. has conducted “intermittent strikes” in Iran but “we’re not fighting right now.” After a month without fighting, Iran and the U.S. traded strikes this week in the Middle East, with Iran also firing at U.S. ally Kuwait. Trump’s categorization came a day after Vice President JD Vance said that he would not describe the conflict with Iran as a war. The president asserted Friday that the U.S. is in control of the Strait of Hormuz and that “we stopped Iran from having a nuclear weapon.” “I don’t think it matters what you call it,” he said. “What matters is the fact that we’ve had tremendous success.” #Trump #Iran #Iranwar #news
